title: Friends
hookLine: a Proverbs magnet on a fridge, and the Buddha's list of four true friends (DN 31)
tomorrow: a list of seven things a friend does. which one is hardest?

lines: A FRIEND LOVETH AT ALL TIMES.
cards: On a kitchen fridge, between a takeout menu and a school photo, there's a magnet with a verse: "A friend loveth at all times, and a brother is born for adversity." That's Proverbs, in the King James words.
It's the kind of line people keep where they'll see it every morning. So does the Buddhist path have a fridge-magnet verse about friends? Not quite a verse.
A whole list, and a direction on a compass.

teach.b: The question is old: how do you tell a true friend from a pleasant one? In the advice to Sigala, the Buddha answers with four kinds of good-hearted friends.

The helper, who looks after you and your things when you're careless, and is a refuge when you're scared. The one who's the same in happiness and sorrow, who keeps your secrets and doesn't leave when trouble comes.

The one who gives good counsel, who steers you off a bad road and tells you what you haven't heard. And the one who cares, who is glad at your good luck, sad at your bad, and speaks up for you when someone runs you down.
In the teaching's map of a life, friends are the north. Now set that beside the fridge.
"A friend loveth at all times" is close kin to the friend who's the same in happiness and sorrow.
"Born for adversity" sounds a lot like the one who doesn't leave when trouble comes. Two traditions, looking hard at the same person, notice the same thing: a friend shows up when it costs something.
Proverbs sits in a book that opens its wisdom with "The fear of the LORD is the beginning of knowledge," so a good friend there lives inside a life turned toward God.
The Sigalovada describes the friend by conduct alone, with no Creator in the frame. Each stands on its own ground.

how: Buddhist teachers often use the Sigalovada's lists of true and false friends in talks for young people and families, and some communities read the whole sutta together.

o: a distraction from the path, to be held loosely
whoever agrees with you and keeps things light
the north on life's map: the people you steer by

games.q: four good-hearted friends — tap the pairs.
p: the same in happiness and sorrow
tells you what you haven't heard
speaks up when you're run down

s: Buddhism says friendship is attachment, so it hardly mentions friends
the Sigalovada lays out four kinds of good-hearted friends in detail.
in the Sigalovada's map of a life, friends are the north
parents are the east, teachers the south, partner and children the west, friends the north.
Proverbs and the Sigalovada say exactly the same thing about friends
both prize the friend at all times; Proverbs frames it within the fear of the LORD, the Sigalovada by conduct alone.

games.q: two friends: one always fun, always agrees with you. one sometimes tells you you're wrong, and stuck by you last winter. by the Sigalovada's list, which one is the north?
o: the fun one; a friend who brings joy is the true friend.
the one who told you hard things and stayed when it cost something.
neither; true friends never disagree and never need to stay.
games.why: the counselor tells you what you haven't heard, and the steady one doesn't leave in trouble. pleasant isn't the same as true.

practice: Think of one friend who fits a line on that list: the helper, the steady one, the counselor, the one who cares. Write them a short thank-you that names the actual thing they did, not just thanks for everything.
Send it now, or keep it ready for later today.

wordCard.voice: Friends: in the Sigalovada, the north, and four kinds of good-hearted friend: helper, steady, counselor, carer.

orig.note: Pali: a friend; the word at the root of metta, friendliness.

carryVoice: The line for today: north, the friends you can steer by. One of six on friends and community.

sources.ref: Digha Nikaya 31 (Sigalovada Sutta: four false friends and four good-hearted friends: the helper, the one the same in happiness and sorrow, the one who gives good counsel, the one who sympathizes; friends as the northern direction)

sources.q: A friend loveth at all times, and a brother is born for adversity.
The fear of the LORD is the beginning of knowledge
